Results.ReviewText:
The Weber E325 grille is the perfect size for us. Small enough for just two or big enough for six or eight. 

The two side tables are very useful, but fold down to tuck away nicely in a corner when you're done. The grille has two burners that will sear your food and then transform back to a three burner grille. 

So far the grille has been great and no need for worrying about dead batteries with new ignition system.
Results.Title: Weber Midsized Gas Grille

Photos.Caption: Spirit with casters and newer model with just wheels on one side.

Results.ReviewText: Purchased a Weber Spirit as we converted to NG and have a smaller patio. Our previous Genesis still worked great after ten years but was just too big for our now smaller home. So we knew we would get another Weber. Purchased it locally as it was the same price as directly from Weber with no shipping fees. It arrived quickly and was easy to assemble, only one brew! We have it a month now and really like how it cooks compared to propane. We like the collapsible side tables, again for a smaller space. The only negative comment is the lack of coaster wheels like other models. Why would Weber do this? It makes it harder to move around when the side table is folded and you have your cover on. It is hard to move without scratching your floor. Does Weber have wheels I could add on??  We plan to have this grill for many years to come! Showing pics of my daughter's with casters and my new NG Spirit.
Results.Title: Love my Weber, but it needs four coaster wheels!

Results.ReviewText: I never enjoyed barbecuing until now! My new Weber BBQ is Amazing!! Heats u quickly…and the temperature gauge is so nice to have on it!  Even heat distribution,  and the sear burners!!!!!OMG!! Absolutely wonderful! It was so easy to assemble.. clear instructions. Good weight to it, not cheaply made like some other brands.  I have never had so much fun cooking before… I’m so in love with this Barbecue ❤️
Results.Title: Excellent BBQ, Buy It!

Results.ReviewText:
This is my first Weber product .. it replaces a 15 year old Ducane propane that had served it's time.  
 I was used to the larger cooking area and stainless grill grates ... The size of the Weber will take some getting used to, especially for when we have company. I have to plan grilling in smaller batches, with backup being kept warm in the house oven.   It's unlikely I will ever be satisfied with the cast iron grates , much bigger downgrade than I expected . 
I like the quality of the frame and grill box and lid .. Cool very visible heat gauge. Also happy with fabric used to make the grill cover and the way it fits... Big plus. Also happy with how well , and fast it reaches cooking temps... heat reflectors and flame tent guards working well so far. 
Ignition lighting took a bit of getting used too and still seem mushy to me  ... don't quite have the  hang of determining if the 'click' did the 'trick', 
I paid $400 at Home depot assembled ... can't help but feeling I got ripped off by about a hundred bucks or so ..  Time will tell, If I get another 15 years for this puppy, all will be forgotten
Results.Title: Treated myself to the Top of the line ?
